transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-21
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Avery Collins (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Karen Liu (Hemisphere Director of AI), Marcus Reed (Hemisphere Platform Eng), Priya Nair (CTO)

Summary/Topics (auto): POC success criteria, workload sizing, bench plan, quality eval (golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination/format checks), data access and security.

[00:00] Avery Collins: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — kind of heavy agenda but we'll try to keep it tight. I'm Avery, AE at Redwood, and Samir's our SE who'll drive the bench.
[00:18] Dr. Karen Liu: Hi, thanks, excited to dig in; we want to validate that model outputs meet clinical note standards and minimize hallucinations — that's our big concern.
[00:28] Samir Patel: Great, quick intro from me. We'll propose a quality eval plan with golden prompts, regression tests, and automatic hallucination/format checks. We'll also run latency & cost benchmarks across a few model variants, incl quantized ones.
[00:40] Priya Nair: Quick constraint from our side — any PII/PHI has to be handled on-prem or via VPC; we can't send live PHI to a third-party public endpoint.
[00:52] Avery Collins: Totally understood. For the POC we usually accept an anonymized sample upload; for production we can do VPC peering or a private deployment. We'll note that as a hard requirement.

[05:12] Marcus Reed: On sizing — for the initial pilot, we're estimating roughly 200k tokens/day (peak), mostly short note summarizations + triage suggestions. Long-term could scale higher. Latency target is sub-500ms for simple prompt/response paths, 95th percentile. Cost sensitivity though — we need to compare hosted vs dedicated.
[05:47] Samir Patel: Good to know. For benching we'll measure 50/80/95th latencies, tokens/sec throughput, and cost per 1k tokens for each model/quantization profile. We'll include a dedicated capacity estimate if you want predictable throughput.

[11:02] Dr. Karen Liu: For quality, our success criteria: clinically accurate summaries (measured via A/B vs ground truth), hallucination rate <2% (we define hallucination as fabricated clinical facts), and formatting correctness (structured JSON note output must validate against our schema).
[11:30] Avery Collins: Nice concrete targets. We'll design the eval to compute precision/recall for key fields, a hallucination detector on entity-level mismatches, and a formatting validator that flags schema failures.

[16:05] Samir Patel: On golden prompts — we recommend creating a set of 200 golden prompts representing typical edge cases: ambiguous notes, conflicting meds, long histories. We'll ask Hemisphere to label expected outputs for a subset (~50) as ground truth. The rest we'll use for regression detection.
[16:42] Marcus Reed: 200 sounds ok. We can produce 500 anonymized segments but we'll label 50 ourselves. Question on regression tests: how often would Redwood run them during the POC?
[16:55] Samir Patel: We can run them daily during the active bench and after any model swap. For the POC we recommend nightly regression runs and a full sweep after any tuning or quantization changes.

[22:20] Priya Nair: Regarding hallucination detection, can you share how automated that is? We can't manually review thousands of outputs.
[22:33] Samir Patel: We'll use a hybrid approach — automated heuristics detect probable hallucinations (entity mismatch, improbable dates) and a sampling-based human review. For initial metric we'll compute automated flags and an estimated false positive/negative rate from the 50 labeled ground truth items.
[22:58] Dr. Karen Liu: So if the auto-detector shows ~3% hallucination but manual says 1.5%, we'll calibrate threshold. We need transparency on detector rules.
[23:10] Avery Collins: Absolutely — we'll include detector rules and examples in the eval doc. Transparency is part of the deliverable.

[29:01] Marcus Reed: On infra — we prefer VPC peering for the pilot. Can Redwood accept an S3 upload behind our VPC or do you need different?
[29:17] Samir Patel: We can accept S3 uploads to a temporary secure bucket, or run a private deployment that reads from your S3 over VPC. For speed we'll probably ask you to upload anonymized samples to an S3 bucket and grant Redwood read-only access for the bench.
[29:35] Priya Nair: Any encryption/KMS requirements?
[29:39] Avery Collins: We support KMS integration and can encrypt at rest. We'll share our KMS integration matrix in the security pack.

[35:02] Dr. Karen Liu: Scoring approach — how will you combine metrics? For us it's not just hallucination but also utility: does the generated summary reduce clinician edit time. Can we include a human-in-the-loop task time measurement?
[35:20] Samir Patel: Yes — we suggest a composite score: weighted sum of hallucination penalty, schema validation rate, and human time-saved estimate (from a small usability study). We'll propose weights but we can make them configurable. Example: score = 0.5*(1 - hallucination_rate) + 0.3*schema_pass_rate + 0.2*time_saved_norm. We'll calibrate with your labeled set.
[35:50] Marcus Reed: That looks reasonable. We might put more weight on hallucination — will discuss offline.

[41:10] Avery Collins: Timelines: we'll share a golden prompt template and the eval spreadsheet tomorrow (2026-03-22). Samir will run a quick baseline (3 model variants: base open model, tuned variant, quantized variant) and send bench + cost by 2026-03-28. Hemisphere provides samples by 2026-03-24. Follow-up to review results week of 2026-03-30. Does that schedule work?
[41:34] Priya Nair: Yes, as long as the data handoff uses our secure upload and we get the security checklist.
[41:42] Avery Collins: We'll send the security checklist and SOC2 docs with the spreadsheet.

[48:05] Samir Patel: Quick technical note on quantization — quantized variants can reduce cost 30–60% but sometimes increase hallucination or formatting errors. We'll include regression tests specifically to check quality delta per quantization profile.
[48:28] Dr. Karen Liu: Important to show that quantized outputs meet our clinical thresholds; otherwise cost savings aren't worth it.
[48:40] Samir Patel: Agreed. We'll tag each run with model config and quantization level and produce side-by-side diffs for the labeled set.

[52:12] Marcus Reed: Anything else on compliance? We may need an executed DPA before sharing sample data — you'll need to confirm the DPA process.
[52:24] Avery Collins: Noted. We'll route that to legal; I'll include a note in the follow-up and attach our DPA template.

[55:00] Priya Nair: Minor nit — for structured output we need strict JSON schema validation and an error-level flag that blocks results that don't conform. Can Redwood's eval pipeline enforce that?
[55:12] Samir Patel: Yes, our pipeline can validate against your schema and mark failures as critical. We'll include a count and example items.
[55:25] Dr. Karen Liu: Perfect.
[55:36] Avery Collins: Recap and next steps: 1) Redwood to send golden prompt template + eval spreadsheet + security checklist + SOC2 by 2026-03-22; 2) Hemisphere to upload 500 anonymized samples and SSO/VPC details by 2026-03-24; 3) Redwood SE to run baseline bench + regression runs and deliver report by 2026-03-28; 4) Follow-up meeting week of 2026-03-30 to review results.
[56:02] Marcus Reed: That works. Also please include clearly documented detector rules and the sample size / confidence intervals for the hallucination estimate.
[56:15] Samir Patel: Will do. We'll also include an appendix with example flagged outputs and manual review notes.
[59:00] Avery Collins: Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and artifacts tomorrow.
[59:10] Dr. Karen Liu: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: occasional transcription noise present (names sometimes mis-transcribed). Links shared: "Eval spreadsheet (link)"; "Redwood security pack (link)".
